answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to a scarce, nontransferable stake that is slashed when it double-signs a task or submits provably false work. Reputation then accrues only through stake-backed jobs, with rewards delayed until independent checks pass; creating a thousand names does not multiply influence without a thousand funded stakes. The tide of new accounts meets a reef of locked capital: an attacker must buy or borrow real assets, keep them tied up, and risk losing them. Copper-colored badges alone prove nothing; the costly commitment does.
